recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recUkfn3htx8gPpK8.Bio: Dave Maybee, sometimes called "the Wizard of Ears," is a holistic practitioner and instructor at the Canadian Institute of Auricular Medicine, known for his work on ear-based diagnostic and energetic healing techniques; he discussed auricular medicine and the ear's fractal anatomy on InnerVerse.
recUkfn3htx8gPpK8.Name: Dave Maybee

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Family Business Born From One German Doctor's Seminar", "body": "Maybee traces his path back about 23 years, to when his mother was dragged to a conference by her partner, a medical doctor, and found a workshop on auricular taught by the German physician Dr. Beatrice Strittmatter. An adult educator by trade, she decided she had to bring the training to Canada, became a practitioner herself and eventually started a school. Maybee, in his early 20s and by his own account directionless, had already self studied anatomy and physiology, went to the seminars because they were free, began assisting, then teaching, and has since taken over the Canadian Institute of Auricular Medicine with his business partner Duvon."}, {"title": "From Otzi's Ear Tattoos To Nogier's Map Of A Baby", "body": "Asked how far back the practice reaches, Maybee says he is not sure anyone has the true answer, but points to very early human remains, including the iceman Chance names as Otzi, carrying tattooed points on the ear that appear to have been used over and over again. He argues it was never a full medicine until Dr. Paul Nogier began looking at the ear as a whole map of the body in the early 1950s, developed it across roughly 20 years, and published in 1972 a chart resembling a baby in fetal position. In that sense, Maybee says, auricular is quite new, and possibly a rediscovery."}, {"title": "Golden Spirals And The Body's Other Microsystems", "body": "Chance opens the show with the observation that the ear may be the most obvious expression of the Fibonacci sequence on the body, a pair of golden spirals sitting on the sides of the head. Maybee agrees, saying the ear is in his mind already designed like a map, a landscape topography set up to orient you, and hazards a guess that far more microsystems exist than we have noticed, naming scalp acupuncture, the abdomen, the hands, the soles of the feet and iridology. He adds that on the chart the hand occupies nearly a fifth of the ear, reflecting nerve density rather than size."}, {"title": "Listening To The Ear Through Somebody's Pulse", "body": "Maybee's favourite form of assessment is pulse guided. Holding the person's pulse and feeling its amplitude, he describes passing a pen, or a substance such as a flower essence, over the ear without contact, and reports that the amplitude grows over an active point. He calls this the VAS, the vascular autonomic signal, and explains it as a very subtle fight or flight response in which the blood vessels all constrict at once, with no delay. He says he registers the same shift in his own pulse, has confirmed students' findings remotely over Zoom, and reads Chance's ear popping during biofield tuning as a related nervous system cue."}, {"title": "Old Traumas As Blockages To Healing", "body": "Whether the picture is tinnitus, chronic pain or migraines, Maybee says he always goes looking for old traumas, what he calls blockages to healing, arguing that anything chronic usually has something underneath maintaining it, sometimes attached to a particular age or body part. He describes vitamin indicator points on the chart, including B12, folic acid and B5, and claims a trauma still live in the nervous system can tether itself to a nutrient. Chance's outro extends the idea with a Rudolf Steiner passage about a train passenger whose memory surfaces unnoticed, and a tuning client whose eleventh birthday fell on September 11, 2001."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dave Maybee, the Wizard of Ears, joins InnerVerse for an educational trip through the fractal mysteries represented on the human ear. As director of the Canadian Institute of Auricular Medicine, Dave combines a variety of modalities with the energetic blueprint of the ear. Tune in to learn more about Auricular history, the ear as a diagnostic window to internal functions, interfacing with the intelligence of the body, the diagram of the ear's correspondence points and DIY ways to work with them, and much more!
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: The Plus+ Extension takes things to philosophical level as we discuss the required commitments for holistic approaches to health, success stories of Auricular medicine, the convergence of Dave's work with psychology, innovative methods for trauma resolution, a profound contemplation on the true nature of memory, the ear as a map of our fetal body, and lasers (for health!).

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Getting Out of the Way of Healing", "body": "Dave says many who find him have tried everything else first, including traditional, rough-around-the-edges people to whom needles in the ear sound crazy. He calls the work a team effort: his part is to identify what stands in the way of healing and stimulate the nervous system to release it, while the person does the allowing. Holding on to old material, he argues, is more work than letting it go. Chance adds that things left to their own devices tend toward order and harmony, that booking a session already signals the decision to heal, and that heading matters more than pace."}, {"title": "Two Medicines Working Together", "body": "Dave's optimism extends to conventional medicine. He would send a bursting appendix, someone in labor or a freshly broken arm straight to the emergency room, and he wishes the allopathic side showed the same humility by handing chronic and lifestyle conditions to holistic practitioners. Chance describes green allopathy, where herbs simply stand in for pharmaceutical pills inside a car repair model of health, and says the real dividing line is understanding that symptoms are symbols. Dave then shares two clinic stories, one where repeat testing overturned a doctor's verdict, and one where his sessions seemingly primed the body for a conventional shot to finally work."}, {"title": "Priming the Nervous System", "body": "Dave likes to treat the ear first because it gives him the lay of the land, such as neck pain really maintained by the sacrum. A craniosacral release his teacher said needed five minutes took thirty seconds once he placed a couple of needles first, which is why he says auricular primes the nervous system to receive other treatments, talk therapy included. He does not practice EMDR himself but helped develop a course pairing it with auricular, and he describes his own method of searching for the points a held memory activates. Chance argues trauma resolves when people see how it conditioned their beliefs and choose a different setting."}, {"title": "Memory Without a Filing Cabinet", "body": "Chance notes that neuroscience has never found a filing cabinet of cells holding any given day, and asks how memory works. Dave sees it as a conditioned response of the nervous system: in nostalgia and PTSD alike, a smell or song recreates an embodied experience rather than a logged file. For him memory carries no timestamp, so part of the nervous system keeps reacting as if the past were still happening, and the work is telling it that it is safe. Chance answers with biofield tuning's tree ring model, where distance from the body marks age, and proposes that memory runs on systems of correspondence, like links in a chain."}, {"title": "The Zero Point, Lasers and the Watermelon", "body": "When critics call auricular medicine pseudoscience, Dave answers with a watermelon: if all you have is a tape measure you will never find its weight, and that does not mean the weight is absent. Asked about the fetal map, he explains the zero point at the center of the ear as the navel, the energetic connection to mother and origin, the solar plexus chakra, and a point for bringing scattered people back to center. He then turns to lasers, which he says feed light directly to the mitochondria so cells can find their own balance, and to adding frequencies that filter an assessment down to one category of points."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "A lot of people think, oh, it's so much work to release old stuff. And my answer to that is actually, it's more work to hang on to the old stuff.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Up to their own devices, things tend towards order and harmony. And so we just gotta find what's blocking that, what's in the way of that.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Sometimes what I'm doing is basically setting up, priming the system for the one intervention that's gonna be the last drop in the bucket.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "What I like to say about auricular is that it primes the nervous system to receive other treatments.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I don't think trauma is necessarily healed just by knowing about it and knowing how it made you feel.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You are creating a response to a unique individual in a unique moment. And not only is that okay, but that's actually the indicator that you're in flow with the source itself.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Once we have a trauma, a lot of times the emotional experience or the nervous system experience of that trauma is being recreated all the time.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If you're trying to find out the weight of a watermelon, but all you have is a tape measure, you're never gonna find the weight of that watermelon.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Do the easy things first, and then the medium things become easy and the hard things become medium.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "What I wanna impress on you is that you have the entire being, access to the entire being, on this really little concise map.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "If we're walking around with a couple of golden spirals on the sides of our head, it seems like that might be a clue that the ear does more than just listen.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "This idea that you could use such a small part of the body as a map of the entire system fascinated me.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "A lot of times blood vessels aren't really very visible on our ears unless it's trying to show us a problem.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "This is my favorite way to listen to the ear is using the pulse of the person because now you're entering into a world of subtlety.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's like the body's intelligence is alive and just waiting for us to figure out how to access it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "So it's a dynamic map also. These points are only gonna be active if and when they represent some activity in the nervous system.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Whether I'm dealing with tinnitus or chronic pain or migraines or anything, anything at all, I always will go looking for old traumas, what I call blockages to healing.", "author": "Dave Maybee", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/dbac8bc6-5a97-4fc6-8f65-2ebb24139965/DAVE-MAYBEE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's lots of parts of the body that are a fractal of the whole. And the body itself is a fractal of the whole. So it's fractals inside of fractals.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
